title: Avdar Market — Google Trends deep dive

data_access.ui_refresh_result: Official Google Trends Explore loaded and exposed its accessible time-series table. A DE five-year Search term control panel for Kaschmirschal vs Wollschal was read successfully; an auxiliary DE Topic panel recognized wool blanket (/g/11bc62qjgl) and Yak-blankets (/g/11kr8j_1fz).
data_access.programmatic_endpoint: The unofficial/internal Explore endpoint returned HTTP 429 outside the browser session. Repeated automated UI panels also began timing out, so no timeout was classified as a true zero.
data_access.collection_route: Official Google Trends Explore in Chrome/CUA; accessible chart tables and related-query panels. No third-party Trends provider.

family_mapping_notes.wool_merino_socks: Wool socks are the inventory/search anchor; merino wording is a language and demand-discovery variant, not a claim that every Avdar sock is merino.
family_mapping_notes.other_blankets: Sheep-wool blanket/throw is the acquisition anchor. Cashmere blanket is preserved as a sparse premium subseries.
family_mapping_notes.shawls: Wool shawl is the main search proxy. Camel-wool shawl exact terms were also checked and were below resolution across the target markets.
family_mapping_notes.yak_blanket: Yak blanket is retained as a separate premium/material family even though the exact Search term series is generally below Trends resolution.

methodology.query_unit: Search-distinct family/material pair; color SKUs were not multiplied.
methodology.query_mode: Literal local Search terms were used for the decision matrix. A plus sign inside one comparison item means OR between close language/word-order variants; commas separate comparison items.
methodology.topic_policy: Use a Topic only when Google exposes a clean category Topic whose scope matches the product family. Do not substitute a generic or product-specific Topic for a material-product query.
methodology.diagnostic_metric: Share of complete weekly observations with index greater than zero. This is an analyst-derived recurrence diagnostic, not an official Google metric and not search volume.
methodology.seasonality_read: The five-year panel establishes recurrence and repeated peak timing. The twelve-month panel checks whether the current cycle still follows the historical shape. A separately normalized 12-month index is not treated as growth versus the five-year index.
methodology.partial_period_policy: The current incomplete week is not used as a standalone signal.

tier_legend.H: Recurring/high-resolution series, generally at least 50% of weekly points non-zero or a continuous strong 12-month series.
tier_legend.0: Below 2%, isolated noise, or below the resolution of the selected panel. This does not prove zero demand.

confidence_legend.high: Stable time series and/or the same conclusion repeats across five-year and twelve-month panels.
confidence_legend.medium: Directional signal is usable but wording, sparse sampling, or panel instability limits precision.
confidence_legend.low: Mostly zeros/isolated spikes, bilingual aggregation, or a dynamic panel did not render consistently.

directional_matrix.interpretation: Wool/merino socks and sheep-wool blankets are the only broadly recurring acquisition families. Cashmere scarves are strongest in DE and PL, testable in DK, and much less resolved elsewhere. Yak blanket, shawl and glove demand should not be sized from Trends alone.

language_formulation_findings.DE: Closed compounds are the default commercial form: Kaschmirschal, Wollschal, Wollsocken, Wollhandschuhe, Wolldecke. Keep Merinosocken and spaced Merino Socken as variants.
language_formulation_findings.NL: Use Dutch kasjmier rather than relying only on English cashmere. For blankets cover both deken and plaid; for socks use wollen sokken with merino sokken as a validated modifier.
language_formulation_findings.BE: Do not use one bilingual panel as a campaign structure. Split NL and FR. For FR blankets, couverture en laine / couverture laine are more natural than only plaid laine; for cashmere scarves include écharpe en cachemire and écharpe cachemire.
language_formulation_findings.DK: Both tørklæde and halstørklæde matter; both cashmere and kashmir spellings should be validated. For blankets, uldplaid and uldtæppe are complementary forms.
language_formulation_findings.SE: Compound/spacing/word-order variants materially change the observed series. Exact kashmirhalsduk and ullhalsduk understate demand relative to kashmir halsduk, cashmere halsduk, ull halsduk and halsduk ull. Use ullsockor + ullstrumpor and ullpläd + ullfilt clusters.
language_formulation_findings.PL: Use accented primary forms and retain unaccented variants for discovery. Szalik and szal are different commercial families; koc is the stronger blanket noun, with pled as secondary. Merino wording appears in rising related searches.
language_formulation_findings.FI: Compound Finnish forms dominate: villasukat, villahuivi, villahuopa, villakäsineet. Cashmere spelling variants remain below resolution, so wording experiments cannot substitute for impression data.

seasonality.five_year_conclusion: The repeated structural pattern is cold-season demand. Wool/merino socks and sheep-wool blankets recur in most markets; scarf and glove peaks are narrower; yak blanket and shawl panels are too sparse for stable seasonality.
seasonality.twelve_month_conclusion: The current cycle preserves the category order seen over five years. No rare premium-material term shows a credible structural breakout. A higher 12-month non-zero share is not proof of growth because Google normalizes each period separately.
seasonality.typical_activation: Late August through September for indexation, landing pages and feed QA; paid-search ramp from late September/October.
seasonality.typical_peak: Mid-November through early December, with socks and blankets often retaining a January tail.

market_nuance.DE: Strongest multi-family search market in the set; scarves, socks and wool blankets all show recurring Q4 signal.
market_nuance.NL: Blankets and socks are more dependable than cashmere scarves or gloves.
market_nuance.BE: Language fragmentation prevents precise seasonal reading for sparse families.
market_nuance.DK: Blankets and socks are reliable; cashmere scarf is a bounded seasonal test.
market_nuance.SE: Socks and blankets are reliable; scarf results are highly spelling-sensitive.
market_nuance.PL: Cashmere/wool scarves, socks, blankets and gloves all show a usable cold-season pattern.
market_nuance.FI: Socks are exceptionally persistent; other literal family terms are much less resolved.

seasonality.ratio_warning: Observed Q4/off-season lifts for strong categories are often roughly 3–8x, but extreme ratios for sparse cashmere/yak terms are denominator artefacts and must not be used as forecasts.

decision_conclusions: Tier 1 search families: wool/merino socks and sheep-wool blankets across the target set, with BE requiring separate NL/FR tests.
Premium scarf priority: DE and PL. DK is a bounded test; NL and BE are conditional localized tests; SE and FI exact series do not support scale assumptions.
Wool scarf is viable in DE, NL and PL; elsewhere it is primarily SEO/attach inventory.
Gloves are a standalone test only in DE and PL; elsewhere use cross-sell and winter merchandising.
Yak blanket and cashmere blanket terms are halo/PDP/remarketing layers, not defensible standalone acquisition families from Trends.
Shawls are vocabulary-fragmented and sparse; sell through editorial/PDP/cross-sell and validate search wording before spend.
Do not use a Google Trends index as searches per month or allocate budgets by comparing index 100 across countries.

contradictions_and_gaps.detail: Any HYPD/Planner-like monthly volume and Trends answer different questions. Trends cannot mathematically validate absolute volume. Agreement is limited to ranking/seasonality where a recurring series exists.
A previously cited absolute estimate of about 260/month is not corroborated by exact kashmirhuivi: the five-year exact series was zero, and spacing/English variants were only about 0.4–0.8% non-zero.
A previously cited absolute estimate of about 590/month is not corroborated by exact kashmirhalsduk (0.8% of five-year weeks); the best word-order/spacing cluster is still only about 8–10%.

An absolute cashmere estimate around 880/month may include broad/close variants. Exact kasjmier sjaal is only 8.8% non-zero over five years and 17.0% over twelve months. Seasonality agrees; scale is not proven.
NL and FR estimates cannot be mechanically added. A bilingual OR panel remains sparse and hides which language drives the signal.

A previously cited absolute estimate around 1,000/month is only weakly reflected by literal villahuopa (12.6% non-zero over five years, 17.0% over twelve months). This may be a broad-match or vocabulary issue and needs Planner/Search Ads evidence.
Exact yak blanket terms and the auxiliary Yak-blankets Topic are below resolution. This is a data gap, not proof that storytelling-led or non-search demand is zero.

Merino variants appear in related/rising queries in DE, NL and PL, but a full stable cross-market merino-only time-series layer was not captured. Do not make a merino fibre claim unless the SKU composition supports it.

The official UI was available on 2026-09-15, but repeated automated panels timed out after the browser session became rate-limited. Those timeouts are recorded as missing measurements, never as zeros.

limitations: Google Trends is sampled and normalized. Each geography/time/query panel is scaled independently so its maximum is 100; the index is not searches per month.
A zero means the sampled value rounded below the panel's resolution, not proven zero demand.
Indices from different panels, countries or time windows must not be added or compared as absolute market sizes.
Low-volume material terms are sensitive to the comparison set: a dominant anchor can cause a small series to round to zero.
Five-year and twelve-month panels are separately normalized. A larger 12-month average/non-zero share is not automatically year-on-year growth.
BE bilingual OR panels improve recall but reduce diagnostic precision; NL and FR must be evaluated separately in Keyword Planner and live Ads tests.
Topics can aggregate languages but may be broader, gender-specific, duplicated or product-specific; Topic and Search term series measure different query universes.
The last week may be incomplete and is not a standalone signal.
Related/rising percentages can come from a very small base; Breakout means greater than 5000% growth, not high absolute volume.
Repeated browser sampling can shift values slightly and can be rate-limited. UI timeouts were recorded as missing rather than zero.
No Google Sheet cells, filters, formulas or metadata were changed.
next_validation_steps: Export Google Ads Keyword Planner by country, language and match type for all primary and alternate terms, especially SE/FI cashmere, BE bilingual categories, FI villahuopa and all yak terms.
Run small exact/phrase live-search tests and record eligible impressions, search-term mix, CTR, CVR and gross-margin contribution by family/language.
Use Search Console and Merchant Center query data to replace Trends zeros with first-party evidence once the localized site/feed is live.
Do not allocate budget from Trends alone; combine recurrence/seasonality with absolute volume, margin, shipping and stock cover.
